title: Workbench becomes hidden canonical store
description: Process identity or runtime data leaks into Workbench metadata or node state because projection shortcuts feel convenient.
mitigation: Keep explicit ADR guardrails, create a dedicated Processes module, and review every Workbench field as projection-only.

title: CanvasLib overreach
description: Process-specific demands force large CanvasLib changes that destabilize Prompt Factory or Project Structure.
mitigation: Start with adapter-level reuse, use group frames as v1 lanes, and phase link-label extensions only when proven necessary.

title: Second scheduling language conflict
description: Process orchestration, project execution context, and future agent-runtime choreography drift apart and create competing models for how work actually flows.
mitigation: Keep Processes canonical for collaboration/handoffs, keep Projects canonical for project scope/context, and use typed links plus PRM-F22/F23 guardrails instead of hidden duplicate scheduling logic.

title: Agent identity duplication outside CRM-HR
description: The process module starts persisting its own durable agent/person records instead of binding to CRM-HR.
mitigation: Make CRM-HR binding mandatory for durable actors and keep process-side identities as references plus snapshots only.

title: SQLite runtime degradation
description: Append-heavy run journals and step events grow faster than expected and SQLite performance drops for large projects.
mitigation: Index project/run/state paths, keep journal append-oriented, define retention/extraction boundaries early, and preserve PostgreSQL parity.

title: Ambiguous transition conditions
description: Decision branches are modeled with free-text conditions that are too vague to test or audit.
mitigation: Separate display text from evaluator metadata, add validation rules, and require reason capture on branch selection.

title: Approval model diverges from future agent rights
description: Process approvals and escalations use shapes that later do not fit AgentFramework permission and approval semantics.
mitigation: Align policy vocabulary now with explicit tool/collaboration/escalation approval concepts and keep a bridge seam rather than runtime coupling.

title: Diagram layout treated as truth
description: Users or coders start inferring semantics from canvas position rather than canonical node/transition data.
mitigation: Store layout separately, make semantic fields explicit, and test import/export without layout dependency.

title: Mermaid round-trip loss
description: Imported or exported Mermaid diagrams lose semantics such as approvals, actor roles, or structured contracts.
mitigation: Import into draft only, emit explicit warnings, keep JSON package as the lossless format, and treat Mermaid as convenience interop.

title: Insufficient audit trail for replay and training
description: Important runtime changes are not journaled, making replay, supervision, and later evaluation incomplete.
mitigation: Define required event types early and verify journal coverage with integration tests and replay tests.

title: Automation before model stability
description: The team tries to fully automate process execution before the base process language and governance model are stable.
mitigation: Prioritize manual and semi-automatic runtime first, then introduce AI executors through a bridge after the core state machine is proven.

title: Cross-module cyclic coupling
description: Process management grows hard references across Projects, CRM-HR, Workbench, Validation, TestLab, Activity, and Automation, making the module brittle.
mitigation: Use narrow bridge interfaces and shared contracts, keep ownership clear, and add integration tests that enforce the intended direction.

title: Advanced parallel orchestration too early
description: Parallel joins, quorum rules, and complex concurrency enter the first waves and slow delivery of the core handoff model.
mitigation: Ship sequential and approval-based handoffs first, postpone advanced parallel constructs to later waves, and keep extension points ready.

title: Shared vs project template confusion
description: Users may not understand whether a process is a global template, a shared project process, or a project-local operational flow.
mitigation: Make scope explicit in the definition model and UI, and separate template promotion from project cloning.

title: Free-text role definitions block staffing reuse
description: Process designers define ad-hoc role names that HR and AI staffing cannot reliably map to templates, skills, or capability expectations.
mitigation: Introduce a governed CRM-HR role/agent template catalog and make free-text exceptions explicit, reviewable, and rare.

title: Self-approval and conflicting duty gaps
description: Approval or assignment rules allow the same actor to both execute and approve sensitive work, weakening governance and audit trust.
mitigation: Model separation-of-duties rules explicitly, validate conflicts before completion/approval, and require audited overrides for exceptions.

title: Capacity-blind staffing and missing fallbacks
description: Assignments ignore availability, validation state, pool eligibility, or backup routes and repeatedly stall or thrash during runtime.
mitigation: Use eligibility rules, capacity-aware candidate search, backup/fallback routes, and durable rebind journaling before critical steps execute.

title: Processes published without real owner or customer
description: The catalog permits important processes to go live without an accountable owner, clear customer, or strategic reason, so responsibility still fragments across departments.
mitigation: Require owner/customer/criticality/value statement before publish and surface stewardship gaps prominently.

title: Activity metrics misused as outcome metrics
description: The implementation reports counts of tasks, approvals, or clicks as success metrics while ignoring lead time, rework, or customer outcome.
mitigation: Model outcome metrics explicitly, split work versus wait time, and prevent dashboards from presenting raw activity as primary KPI.

title: Happy-path modeling hides real exceptions
description: Designers capture only the ideal route and runtime teams keep solving deviations through email, chat, and side agreements.
mitigation: Make variants, exception paths, override reasons, and conformance observations first-class; review repeated deviations regularly.

title: Process change sprawl and unofficial forks
description: Versioning exists technically, but real process change is still communicated informally and multiple live variants emerge without governance.
mitigation: Introduce governed change proposals, impact analysis, communication/acknowledgement, and prioritization tiers for which changes need stronger control.

title: Over-control creates process bureaucracy
description: The team adds controls and approvals to every path, slowing low-risk work and causing users to bypass the official process.
mitigation: Use risk-tiered controls, explicit decision rights, and regular control rationalization reviews to remove unnecessary gates.

title: Observation data becomes gossip or privacy liability
description: Conformance or field-observation tooling stores ungoverned rumor-like notes about people instead of structured operational evidence.
mitigation: Keep observation capture structured, access-controlled, and focused on execution evidence, deviation patterns, and approved governance review only.

title: Dual template systems diverge
description: CRM-HR role or agent templates and runtime-side AgentFramework templates drift into conflicting sources of truth for staffing and execution.
mitigation: Keep CRM-HR canonical, snapshot only bridge hints into runtime contracts, and verify convergence through adapter tests.

title: Direct agent wiring bypasses the process
description: Teams connect agents directly to each other or to tools outside modeled process steps, hiding responsibility changes, approvals, and customer-facing done criteria.
mitigation: Introduce process-native work briefs and baton artifacts, require override journaling for break-glass paths, and review hidden collaboration shortcuts.

title: Provider and capability registry duplication
description: AgentFramework overlay registries continue independently from CanDoItAll Workspace provider profiles and shared capability proof rules.
mitigation: Define explicit convergence rules, keep Workspace and shared capability ownership canonical, and forbid new permanent registries in the bridge layer.

title: Runtime sessions become orphaned from process context
description: AI execution sessions, logs, or metrics exist but cannot be tied back to the process run, step, assignment, or owner that triggered them.
mitigation: Require process-bound correlation identifiers and external execution link records before future adapters are approved.

title: Canvas runtime overlay is mistaken for canonical state
description: Developers or users assume live canvas overlays are the source of truth and start mutating process state through projection shortcuts.
mitigation: Keep overlay services read-only over canonical stores, mark projections explicitly in UI, and add tests that reject projection-only mutations.
